note: Two blackened vertical-timber volumes with angular black-framed glazing step down a slope, snow banked on their flat eaves, a snow-hazed spruce hillside rising behind and a flat pale sky filling the top third; no people, cars, signage or text anywhere in frame.
why: It is the brief's exact material story — charred/blackened timber cladding plus glass, set among conifers — rendered in a genuine near-monochrome of true black, charcoal, snow-white and desaturated forest green, with a large quiet sky band at the top edge for headline type, matching the panel's established treatment.

note: sculptural white timber studio with a folded cantilevered roof on bare coastal rock above a grey North Atlantic
why: replaces the midday turquoise brochure shot with flat overcast light and a stone/white/ochre palette; a single sculptural modernist volume, deep calm negative space in sky and foreground heath

note: A flat sand-ochre plaster wall cut by one narrow vertical void that reads as pure black, with a single hard-edged diagonal shadow crossing the lower half; no people, no signage, no sky.
why: It is the most severe and monolithic frame in the pool — sand-toned, near-monochrome, long raking shadow, deep true black in the aperture — and its extreme simplicity (entropy 5.35) survives the panel's +5deg rotation and heaviest at-rest blur while leaving two large quiet fields for headline type.

note: long glazed pavilion glowing warm amber behind snow-covered boulders and bare trees at blue hour
why: cold blue snow light against one warm glazed wall, exactly the brief's single-light-source reading; deep dusk sky rather than saturated daytime blue, and no people, cars or signage
